attempts.note: Vendor-published OpenAPI 3.0.0 behind the docs.browserless.io API reference (Browserless Enterprise and Cloud, v2.60.0): 92 paths / 106 operations / 88 schemas
the running server's /docs and /openapi.json need a token (HTTP 401); the docs-site copy is the same vendor document without auth

open-source repo generates static/docs/swagger.json at build time (scripts/build-open-api.js) and does not commit it; raw main-branch paths 404. The OSS container API is a subset of the Enterprise/Cloud spec used here

cross-check only: every /rest-apis/* reference page (pdf, screenshot, content, scrape, function, download, export, performance, unblock, crawl, map, search, smart-scrape, scrapers, batch-scrape, agent-run) maps to a path in the spec

notes: Browserless is a hosted (and self-hostable) headless-browser service. upstream.json is the vendor's own OpenAPI 3.0.0 document served from docs.browserless.io (Browserless Enterprise and Cloud v2.60.0), saved verbatim; openapi.json equals it plus info.x-openfn-adaptor and one mechanical normalisation: 9 draft-07 tuple-form `items: [..]` arrays (all inside the GET /chromium/agent/capabilities response) are rewritten as `items: {anyOf: [..]}`, because an array-valued `items` is invalid in OpenAPI 3.0 and fails the conformance engine's schema compile; only positional ordering is lost. upstream.json is untouched, and re-running `pnpm specs convert browserless` would drop this rewrite. It replaces a 4-operation docs-authored stub and covers 106 operations: REST APIs (pdf, screenshot, content, scrape, function, download, export, performance, unblock, search, map, smart-scrape, crawl, batch-scrape, agent runs), profiles, sessions, 1Password integration, BrowserQL, and the WebSocket/CDP connect endpoints (documented as GET paths). The adaptor's createPDF calls POST /pdf (default base https://production-sfo.browserless.io, token as a query parameter, matching the tokenAuth scheme); it is present. The real /pdf and /screenshot responses are binary (application/pdf, image/*), as the upstream says; the adaptor base64-encodes the PDF onto state.data, which the spec does not model. Vendor paths use router globs (/browser/*, /kill/+([0-9a-zA-Z-_]), /chromium/bql?(/*)) rather than {param} templates and many operations lack operationId; kept as published.
